title: Pressed Cuban Sandwiches for the Crew
displayTitle: Pressed Cuban Sandwiches for the Crew
seoTitle: Pressed Cuban Sandwiches for the Crew | Firehall BBQ
shortDescription: Cuban press night—roast pork, ham stack, griddle-crisp bread for ten
subtitle: Roast pork, ham, Swiss, pickles, and mustard on pressed Cuban bread for ten
description: Marinated roast pork shoulder grills and slices, layers with ham, Swiss, pickles, and mustard on Cuban bread, and presses on the griddle until shatter-crisp.

steps.title: Mojo-marinate pork
steps.instruction: Rub pork shoulder with sour orange, garlic, oregano, and salt. Marinate at least 4 hours. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Use deli ham as listed — measure each before heat goes on. Target 145°F with a 3-minute rest at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Grill roast pork
steps.instruction: Grill pork over medium 400°F, turning, until 195°F internal for slicing, about 90 minutes total. Rest and slice thin. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 145°F with a 3-minute rest at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Hold sliced pork
steps.instruction: Hold sliced pork covered at 170°F in hotel pans until sandwich build. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 145°F with a 3-minute rest at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Build cubans
steps.instruction: Spread mustard on bread. Layer ham, Swiss, pickles, and sliced pork. Butter outside of bread. Keep finished cold items below 41°F if they sit more than 30 minutes — nest the hotel pan on ice at the line. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early. Target 145°F with a 3-minute rest at the thickest point before moving to the next batch.

steps.title: Preheat the flat-top griddle
steps.instruction: Preheat griddle to 375°F for pressing. Plan about 8 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Press sandwiches
steps.instruction: Press cubans with weight 4 minutes per side until bread is flat, crisp, and cheese melts. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Hold wrapped
steps.instruction: Hold pressed cubans wrapped in foil at 170°F up to 25 minutes. Hold covered at 140°F up to 20 minutes — log the time if your hall tracks food safety during long shifts. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Line for ten
steps.instruction: One cuban per firefighter. Cut diagonal before serving. Plan about 5 minutes for this step at crew scale. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

proTips: 195°F pork shoulder slices thin and juicy—don't pull early.
Press with real weight—a spatula alone won't shatter the crust.
Pickles and mustard balance rich pork and ham fat.
tonightSpread: Pressed Cuban sandwiches with plantain chips.
Black beans and rice on the side.
leftovers: Cuban halves re-crisp on griddle next day.
Pork slices into rice bowls with mojo.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Cubans are a complete meal in one press. Pork grills ahead and holds at 170°F; sandwiches press in batches when the crew sits.
mealPrepNotes: Grill pork at 400°F to 195°F for slicing. Hold pork at 170°F up to 45 minutes. Press sandwiches at 375°F, 4 minutes per side with weight.
